clue.text: Objection with pressure losing initial support

indicators.note: losing its initial means the word gives up its first letter and goes in without it

blocks.note: 'but' is a word used to raise an objection, as in 'no buts'
stress is pressure or strain

explanation.surface: An objection raised under pressure loses the first bit of backing it had.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttress is a projecting structure built against a wall to prop it up, so it is a physical support.

clue.text: Church building I left, entering unadorned area

indicators.note: the words before go into the word that follows, the way someone enters a room

blocks.note: basic means plain, without frills
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a church and walked into a bare open space.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church with a nave and aisles, or one given special status by the Pope.

clue.text: Plant becomes brown and crinkly, finally

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each word it governs, the very end only

blocks.note: tan is a light brown
the last letter of this word
the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A plant at the end of its life turns brown and wrinkled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becomes' looks like a link, but finally applies to it as well as to crinkly, giving the last letter of each.
explanation.definitionFit: Tansy is a yellow-flowered herb of the daisy family, once used in cooking and medicine.

clue.text: Describe requirement after close vote

blocks.note: first meaning: to narrate or tell an account of something
second meaning: a second tally of ballots, demanded when the result is very narrow

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to narrate events in detail, and the noun is a fresh tally of votes demanded when a result is tight.

clue.text: Call universe complicated, making observation

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An astronomer calls the cosmos intricate after looking at the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveillance is close watching of a person or place, especially by police or spies, so it is observation.

clue.text: Pair with one child in place of captivity

blocks.note: PR is the standard abbreviation for pair
the Roman numeral for one
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A couple with their only child are stuck somewhere they cannot leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison is a jail, an institution where people are held captive as punishment.

clue.text: Temperature wrong in most of actual wine

indicators.note: in places the first two items inside the shortened word, sitting within it
most of a word means all but its last letter is kept

blocks.note: real means actual; most of it drops the last letter
T is the abbreviation for temperature
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: The serving temperature is wrong for most of a real wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a resin-flavoured Greek white wine, so it is a specific kind of wine.

clue.text: Number watched gripping episode

indicators.note: gripping means holding tightly, so the first word clasps the second inside itself

blocks.note: seen means watched or viewed
an event is an episode or occurrence

explanation.surface: A viewer counts how many times they sat through an exciting instalment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripping episode' reads as an exciting instalment; gripping is the container signal, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventeen is a cardinal figure, ten plus seven, so it is a number.

clue.text: Edges of notice, somewhat loose, curl up

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outside letters, first and last, with the middle dropped

blocks.note: first and last letters of this word
first and last letters of this word
first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A notice comes slightly unstuck and its corners curl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges of' covers all three following words, not just notice; 'somewhat' is not a hidden-word signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle snugly and comfortably, as when one curls up against a cushion.

clue.text: Satisfied about arrangement of nice easy job

indicators.note: an arrangement sets things out in a new order, so the following word's letters are reordered
about means around, so the satisfied word goes round the rearranged letters

blocks.note: to be sure is to be satisfied, convinced
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is content with a pleasant, undemanding work set-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post requiring little or no work, the classic cushy number.

clue.text: Parts of barrels, tons in stores

indicators.note: in puts the tons inside the word for stores, like goods kept in a warehouse

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tons
to store something is to save it up

explanation.surface: Bits of barrels are kept by the ton in warehouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Staves are the curved wooden strips that a cooper fits together to form the sides of a cask.

clue.text: Mock actor's words about struggle with singular lack of courage

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mock word is wrapped around the struggle

blocks.note: cod is British slang for fake or mock, as in cod philosophy
a war is a struggle
an actor learns lines
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A parody of a performer's script about combat in which one man shows no nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: Cod as an adjective is British slang for imitation or sham.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardliness is the quality of being a coward, the absence of bravery or nerve.

clue.text: Put down narrative poem

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of the verb to set something down
second meaning: a short ballad or song telling a story

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses or sets aside a story told in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of the verb meaning to place something, and also a medieval term for a sung story in verse.

clue.text: Revolutionary book in harmony with a line that's cool

indicators.note: a revolution is a full turn, so the book word is turned round end to end
in places the turned book word inside the word for harmony

blocks.note: a tome is a large book
union is agreement or harmony
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A radical book that agrees with a fashionable party line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary book' reads as a political manifesto, but it is a book turned round, placed inside harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cool in temperament is calm and detached, showing no feeling, which is what unemotional means.

clue.text: Shout by old man in stand, great for football club

indicators.note: in puts the old man inside the stand, like a father standing in a booth

blocks.note: to cry out is to shout
a stall is a market stand
one's old man is one's father, pa
ace is slang for great, excellent

explanation.surface: A dad bellowing from the terraces is just the thing for a soccer team.
explanation.walkthrough: Crystal Palace is a London football club. The surface stand is the grandstand, but here it is a market stall wrapped round the father.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal Palace is an English professional football club based in south London, nicknamed the Eagles.

clue.text: Standard criticism after cart overturned

indicators.note: a cart that is overturned is flipped over, so the word for it reads from the end in this down entry

blocks.note: a dray is a low flat cart for heavy loads
to give someone stick is to criticise them

explanation.surface: A cart flips over and the usual complaints follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Stick is informal British for harsh criticism. 'After' places it behind the reversed cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a measure or benchmark against which other things are judged.

clue.text: Device controlling engine's power in time, hot and dry in part

indicators.note: the second in sets dry inside the word for part, sitting within it

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
a role is a part in a play
TT, teetotal, describes someone who stays off alcohol

explanation.surface: A description of an engine part under heat and without lubrication.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry here means not drinking, abbreviated TT for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A throttle is the valve that regulates fuel or air flow to an engine, governing its output.

clue.text: Complete reconstruction of barn to do with farm

indicators.note: a reconstruction rebuilds something in a new form, so the letters are put together again differently

blocks.note: the letters to be rebuilt
a ranch is a large farm

explanation.surface: A full rebuild of the barn, all part of the farm's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A root-and-branch change is thorough and radical, reaching every part, so it is total.

clue.text: Work, fashionable one concerning belief

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
in means in fashion
the Roman numeral for one
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A trendy piece of writing about someone's faith.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or judgement held about something, a personal conviction.

clue.text: Conducted tribunal without ending bitterness

indicators.note: without its ending means the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to run something is to conduct or manage it
a court is a tribunal

explanation.surface: A hearing was run that left the parties resentful forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is long-lasting resentment or ill feeling, a deep-seated grudge.

clue.text: Run into trouble, then appeal? That's clever

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the run abbreviation is put within the trouble word

blocks.note: ado is fuss or trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Getting into difficulty and then lodging an appeal: a smart move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run into trouble' reads as a phrase meaning get into difficulty, but run goes inside trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and quick-witted, deft in handling a situation.

clue.text: Contrast in excellence

blocks.note: first meaning: a difference drawn between two things
second meaning: outstanding merit, as in a pass with honours

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a difference noted between things and the quality of being outstanding or eminent.

clue.text: Speak softly? Successful move in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as it reaches the ear, so the clue word is judged by its sound alone

blocks.note: a coup is a brilliant, successful stroke; the P is silent

explanation.surface: Whispering about a winning stroke so that it is overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: COUP comes from French and is said without its P, so it sounds the same as the dove's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To coo is to murmur gently and tenderly, like a dove or a doting parent.

clue.text: Series about hospital patient with odd parts omitted

indicators.note: leaving out the odd-numbered letters keeps only the second, fourth and sixth of the word

blocks.note: C is short for circa, about
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
the even letters, second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A succession of stories about a hospital patient, with strange bits left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain is a connected sequence of linked things, as in a chain of events.

clue.text: Beginning to rig inquiry partially

indicators.note: partially means only in part, so the answer is a piece taken from inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Starting to fix the result of an investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to' looks like 'starting to', but the definition is just the noun Beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the point where something starts, its source or commencement.

clue.text: Vibrant instinct reflected in angry speech

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the instinct word is read backwards
in sets the turned instinct word inside the word for angry speech

blocks.note: a nose for something is an instinct for it
a rant is a loud angry tirade

explanation.surface: A lively gut feeling is mirrored in a furious tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant sound is deep, full and reverberating, so it is vibrant in tone.

clue.text: Cheers ruler is receiving

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thank you
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch toasted at a reception, glass raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a gift or payment is the same as accepting or getting it, both present participles.

clue.text: Alienate sergeant in disorder

indicators.note: in disorder means jumbled and out of place, so the letters of the rank are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Pushing away an NCO whose ranks are in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to make them hostile or distant, cutting them off as a friend.
